title: Console backend: route-level quantization settings endpoints + compatibility validation + audit records
author: Chloe Martin
release_notes:
- Adds Console backend APIs for viewing and updating route-level quantization profile settings (opt-in, feature-flagged).
- Adds server-side compatibility validation and user-facing warning/error mapping.
- Emits structured audit events for enable/disable and profile ref changes.
body: Summary: Adds the Console backend surface area needed for route-level Quantization Profile Library enablement. Specifically: (1) endpoints to display available profile options for a route/model, (2) a server-side compatibility/guardrail validation path that mirrors policy engine rules (with explicit dry-run support for UI previews), and (3) write endpoints that persist changes via the control plane config service and emit audit records with diffs. Motivation: Console needs a single backend façade that can (a) call into control-plane resolution/validation, (b) map errors into UX-friendly messages, and (c) ensure RBAC + auditable change history. This PR does not change serving defaults; routes remain baseline precision unless explicitly configured. API details: GET /console/v1/routes/{route_id}/quantization-settings -> returns current effective setting (disabled|default|profile_ref), global kill-switch state (read-only), and last-change metadata (actor + timestamp when available). GET /console/v1/routes/{route_id}/quantization-profiles/options?region=&deployment_tier= -> returns list of eligible profiles for the route’s pinned model version, including profile_id, label (stable/experimental), expected savings fields when available, and compatibility status. POST /console/v1/routes/{route_id}/quantization-settings -> accepts quantization_profile_ref (or "default"), enabled boolean, optional region/deployment_tier selectors, and dry_run=true to return validation warnings without persisting. Guardrails/validation: Validation is performed by calling the control plane quantization config service (single request) which evaluates compatibility (model family/variant, GPU SKU class, max context constraints) and returns either OK, OK_WITH_WARNINGS, or INCOMPATIBLE with machine codes; backend maps to UI-safe messages and includes remediation hints (e.g., "select baseline" or "choose a profile compatible with L4 class"). RBAC: Adds permission gate console.routes.write_quantization (requires routes:write + quantization:manage). Read endpoints require routes:read. Audit: Write path emits QUANT_PROFILE_SETTINGS_CHANGED audit events including actor, route_id, old/new setting, and selectors (region/tier). Audit emission is best-effort but failure to write audit fails the request (per security review guidance) to avoid untracked changes. Performance: Options endpoint caches resolved profile option metadata for 30s per (route_id, selectors) to avoid thundering herds on model registry reads during Console refreshes. Tests: Adds unit tests for request validation and error mapping; adds integration tests with mocked control-plane responses (OK / warning / incompatible / kill-switch). Notes: Console UI work in ENG-5818 will consume these endpoints. Related: PR-18445 (control plane CRUD) and PR-18488 (kill-switch propagation).
commits: console-backend: add route quantization settings service client + request/response models
api: implement GET quantization-settings endpoint (effective state + last-change metadata)
api: implement GET quantization profile options endpoint with selector support + caching
api: implement POST quantization-settings write endpoint with dry_run validation
rbac: add console.routes.write_quantization permission gate + tests
audit: emit QUANT_PROFILE_SETTINGS_CHANGED events with diff fields + failure semantics
docs: update internal OpenAPI annotations + example payloads
tests: add unit + integration coverage for compatibility error mapping and kill-switch handling
review_conversation: Ethan Park: Can we guarantee we’re not duplicating policy-engine compatibility logic here? I’d prefer the Console backend call the control-plane validation endpoint and not re-implement SKU/model checks in this repo.

Chloe Martin (author): Yep—no local compatibility rules. The backend calls the control-plane validate/resolve endpoint and only maps machine codes -> UI copy + remediation. Added a test asserting we don’t branch on gpu_sku/model fields beyond pass-through.
Jada Williams: Audit diff needs to include old/new quantization_profile_ref *and* enabled flag. Also please include selectors in the diff (region/deployment tier) since those affect blast radius.

Chloe Martin (author): Updated audit payload to include old/new for enabled + profile_ref + selectors. Also switched to failing the write if audit emission fails to avoid untracked changes (aligned with Naomi’s note below).
Naomi Feldman: RBAC: read endpoints can be routes:read but write must require an explicit quantization permission. We’ve been burned by broad routes:write before.
Chloe Martin (author): Added console.routes.write_quantization gate (routes:write + quantization:manage). Updated error response to return 403 with a stable error_code for the Console UI.

Dylan Brooks: For the options endpoint, we should support dry-run previews the UI can call before the confirmation modal. Does POST dry_run cover this? Also please ensure the response includes warnings in a structured way.

Chloe Martin (author): Yes—POST supports dry_run=true and returns warnings[] + warning_codes[]. Also added GET options to include per-profile compatibility status so the dropdown can gray out incompatible items without an extra call.
Benji Okafor: Please ensure caching doesn’t bypass kill-switch updates. If kill-switch flips, UI should immediately reflect "disabled" and block writes.

Chloe Martin (author): Cache key now includes kill_switch_version from control plane; if it changes, cache is bypassed. Write path always checks kill-switch live and returns 409 error_code=QUANT_PROFILES_GLOBALLY_DISABLED.
CI (openapi-schema-lint): failed on missing response schema for 409; author added schema + examples; re-run passed.
Approvals: Ethan Park approved after validation path confirmed; Naomi Feldman approved after RBAC changes; Jada Williams approved after audit diff update; Dylan Brooks approved.
deployment_notes: Feature-flagged behind console.quant_profiles_route_settings (default off). No DB migrations in Console backend. Requires control plane quantization config service endpoints from PR-18445 to be deployed first. Verify in staging: (1) GET settings returns disabled by default, (2) POST dry_run returns warning/incompatible codes, (3) POST write emits audit event and the change is visible in audit log explorer, (4) toggling global kill-switch causes POST to return 409 with QUANT_PROFILES_GLOBALLY_DISABLED and GET settings reflects disabled state.
